title: High-quality RNA extraction from zebrafish tissue
author: Stephen Carter

steps.title: Collect and stage embryos
steps.instruction: Collect zebrafish embryos, allowing each pair of fish to mate for exactly 5 minutes, then raise embryos to the desired developmental stage (e.g., 0–1 dpf). Choose whole‑animal extraction or dissection/FACS as required.

steps.title: Add Trizol to samples
steps.instruction: Keep all samples on ice, place each in an Eppendorf tube and add 500 µL of Trizol reagent. Samples may be frozen at –80 °C at this point for later extraction.

steps.title: Homogenize samples
steps.instruction: Homogenize each sample by repeatedly aspirating through a G30 needle attached to a 1 mL syringe; be vigorous without causing the tube to overflow, and allow generous foaming.

steps.title: Recover aqueous phase
steps.instruction: Carefully transfer the upper aqueous phase to a new tube, avoiding contact with the interphase and organic phase; leave any residual aqueous phase behind if necessary.

steps.title: Filter ethanol solutions
steps.instruction: Filter the 96–99 % ethanol and 70 % ethanol solutions through a 0.2 µm filter and store the filtered solutions in the freezer until use.

steps.title: Dry and resuspend RNA
steps.instruction: Air‑dry the pellet until all ethanol has evaporated (do not over‑dry), then resuspend in 30–50 µL distilled water and store at –80 °C. The RNA is now ready for QC, RNA‑seq, or other applications.
